canonical_definition:
What it is. Across papers, the prevailing usage treats OpenBookQA, also written as OpenbookQA or OBQA, as a multiple-choice, open-book question answering benchmark or dataset, usually centered on elementary science questions and modeled after open-book exams. Most definitions say it requires reasoning over a provided set or small corpus of science facts together with common, external, or broad common knowledge; several papers further describe it as testing factual and commonsense reasoning, and some call it multi-step or multi-hop reasoning. A smaller set of papers instead frames it as open-domain QA, reading comprehension, or book comprehension. Descriptions also differ on size and placement: one paper says it contains 500 multiple-choice questions, another says it comprises 5,957 multiple-choice questions with four options, and one paper treats OBQA as a subset of VoiceBench.

What it is claimed to measure. Papers connect OpenBookQA to 12 constructs and 10 behavioral indicators. The dominant claim is that papers use it to measure Commonsense reasoning; recurring but less concentrated claims say it measures General ability, Generalization, Reasoning, and Calibration, so the claims center on one construct but also extend across several others. At the behavioral level, it is reported as measuring Question answering, Language understanding task performance, Multiple-choice question answering, Machine reading comprehension, and Classification.

Space of uses. Most papers position OpenBookQA as one task in broader benchmark bundles, often alongside PIQA, HellaSwag, and ARC-Easy/ARC-Challenge, and they commonly report accuracy in zero-shot evaluations. A smaller line of work fine-tunes on it, uses it as an additional training task, or treats it as a held-out or validation benchmark for generalization. Papers also report that OpenBookQA is measured by 2 other instruments, most often lm-evaluation-harness, with a smaller mention of OLMES.

characterization_sections.label: What it is.
characterization_sections.text: Across papers, the prevailing usage treats OpenBookQA, also written as OpenbookQA or OBQA, as a multiple-choice, open-book question answering benchmark or dataset, usually centered on elementary science questions and modeled after open-book exams. Most definitions say it requires reasoning over a provided set or small corpus of science facts together with common, external, or broad common knowledge; several papers further describe it as testing factual and commonsense reasoning, and some call it multi-step or multi-hop reasoning. A smaller set of papers instead frames it as open-domain QA, reading comprehension, or book comprehension. Descriptions also differ on size and placement: one paper says it contains 500 multiple-choice questions, another says it comprises 5,957 multiple-choice questions with four options, and one paper treats OBQA as a subset of VoiceBench.

characterization_sections.label: What it is claimed to measure.
characterization_sections.text: Papers connect OpenBookQA to 12 constructs and 10 behavioral indicators. The dominant claim is that papers use it to measure Commonsense reasoning; recurring but less concentrated claims say it measures General ability, Generalization, Reasoning, and Calibration, so the claims center on one construct but also extend across several others. At the behavioral level, it is reported as measuring Question answering, Language understanding task performance, Multiple-choice question answering, Machine reading comprehension, and Classification.

characterization_sections.label: Space of uses.
characterization_sections.text: Most papers position OpenBookQA as one task in broader benchmark bundles, often alongside PIQA, HellaSwag, and ARC-Easy/ARC-Challenge, and they commonly report accuracy in zero-shot evaluations. A smaller line of work fine-tunes on it, uses it as an additional training task, or treats it as a held-out or validation benchmark for generalization. Papers also report that OpenBookQA is measured by 2 other instruments, most often lm-evaluation-harness, with a smaller mention of OLMES.
